subject: French

source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design — French Grade 7 (First published 2022, Revised 2024)
source.notes: Read in full via the Read tool (no pages param). Backfilled retroactively — skills already shipped in web/src/skills/frenchG7/ before this record was written. Structure verified verbatim against the PDF's own SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB STRANDS table (page x) and the per-theme strand tables (pages 1-43): 3 strands (Listening and Speaking, Reading, Writing) x 9 themes = 27 sub-strands, matching the frenchG7 skill folder's 9 themes x 3 skills (Speaking/Reading/Writing) each. Essence statement identical in spirit to Grade 8: Kenya's foreign languages at Junior School are Arabic, French, German and Mandarin, non-formal basic (A1/YCT2-equivalent) 4-skills curriculum guided by social-constructivism and environmental theories. Total suggested lessons: 27 (Listening & Speaking) + 18 (Reading) + 9 (Writing) = 54, plus 6 lessons for showcasing.

essenceNote: Kenya is part of the international community and the learner is given an opportunity to learn foreign languages (Arabic, French, German, Mandarin) in addition to national/official/indigenous languages, acquiring the four language skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing) at a basic level in a non-formal curriculum, guided by social-constructivism and environmental theories, transiting to senior school with basic proficiency equivalent to A1/YCT2 (verbatim essence statement).

subStrands.name: Interactive Speaking — Informal and Other Forms of Greetings
specificLearningOutcomes: Respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement
Use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions
Use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication
Exhibit confidence to contribute actively in conversations
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you communicate without talking?
learningExperiences: Listen to audio material on informal greetings and respond to prompts
Listen to and sing songs with vocabulary on informal greetings and introductions
Participate in simple skits on greetings and introductions while speaking clearly and effectively using appropriate language expressions and gestures
Source and watch video clips with dialogues on introductions with a view to appreciate diversity (Comment tu t'appelles ? Quel âge as-tu ? Tu habites où ? Et ton ami/amie ?)
Participate in "Repeat-after-me" exercise to acquire vocabulary (salut, coucou, ça marche, ça roule, ça gaze ! quoi de neuf ?)
Play mimicry games such as charades and mirroring jointly to acquire non-verbal communication skills
linkedLearningAreas: The concept of informal greetings and introduction is linked to the greetings concept in social linguistics in Kiswahili
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: developed as the learner speaks clearly and effectively using appropriate language expression and gestures while presenting skits
Creativity and Imagination: as the learners undertake communication using non-verbal cues
values: Respect: as the learners appreciate the diversity in names, age and where they live
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Citizenship: Social cohesion is enhanced as learners engage in mimicry activities in groups

subStrands.name: Oral Expression — Nuclear Family
specificLearningOutcomes: Use varied vocabulary when speaking
Employ fluency in verbal communication
Express enthusiasm in oral communication
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is family important?
learningExperiences: Outline vocabulary on members of a nuclear family
Listen to audiovisual texts of people presenting their families (name, age and professions)
Present role plays on members of family asking and presenting on name, age and professions with emphasis on speaking clearly and effectively using appropriate language, expressions and gestures
Carry out short exposés of different family models with emphasis on appreciating diversity and uniqueness
linkedLearningAreas: As the learners engage in role plays they are able to relate the skill of acting with drama in Creative Arts
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: learners speak clearly and effectively using appropriate language, expressions and gestures in role plays
Digital Literacy: as learners manipulate digital devices as they listen to audiovisual texts on members' families names, age and professions
values: Respect: as learners recognize the uniqueness of each family and accommodate the differences while presenting the exposés on different family models
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Self-esteem: Learners acquire self-esteem as they talk about themselves and their families as they present exposés on different family models

subStrands.name: Interactive Listening — The Market
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify key points from audio stimuli
Ask and give information in oral interactions
Value the importance of paying attention to details while listening
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do people make a shopping list?
learningExperiences: Identify different types of shops in the market from images (boucherie, épicerie, boutique...)
Ask for the locations of different shops in the market (où est ? où se trouve ?...)
Listen to audio-visual materials and pick vocabulary and expressions on selling and buying at the market (expressions de quantité: nombres, litre, kilo...)
Ask for prices of items in different shops in the market using polite language in order to make informed choices (polite form: Je voudrais...) (ça coûte combien / ça fait combien, s'il vous plaît...)
Use the vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures to describe items in a shop at the market
Simulate simple dialogues on buying and selling at the market as they compare prices
Create a shopping list to guide them when buying items at the market
linkedLearningAreas: The concept of creating a shopping list is linked to financial literacy in Business Studies under Pre-technical Studies
coreCompetencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: as the learners compare prices to make informed choices on what to buy
values: Respect: as learners learn to ask for prices of items politely when shopping
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Financial Literacy: as the learners use a shopping list to buy at the market

subStrands.name: Active Listening — Important Dates
specificLearningOutcomes: Recall details and information accurately from oral interactions
Interpret verbal cues from audio stimuli
Demonstrate willingness to be receptive to new ideas in oral interactions
keyInquiryQuestions: Are some dates more important than others?
learningExperiences: Play number games to work on dates
Practice asking and saying the date: (Quelle est la date aujourd'hui? C'est lundi le 4 janvier, 2024)
Participate in rhyming games to acquire vocabulary on important dates (date d'anniversaire, nouvel an, noël, fêtes nationales)
Watch audio-visual clips with important dates
linkedLearningAreas: Learning important dates can be linked to the concept of national holidays in Social Studies
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: as learners listen keenly and actively as they participate in asking and saying the date
values: Patriotism: as learners value the important dates of national holidays through participating in rhyming games
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Self-awareness: as learners share about their individual birthdays and important dates in their lives

subStrands.name: Listening for Information — Leisure Time
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify key points from audio stimuli
Use information from audio stimuli to respond to questions or prompts
Cultivate awareness on the importance of paying attention to details when listening for information
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should we create time for fun and enjoyment?
learningExperiences: Pick out aspects of time when leisure time activities take place from audiovisual texts (après les cours, récréation, week-ends, vacances)
Listen keenly and respond appropriately to questions on when they engage in leisure time activities
Play word puzzle games with vocabulary on leisure activities
Watch short video clips on leisure activities in Kenya and elsewhere
Come up with a list of leisure activities that promote healthy living
Discuss on leisure time activities that they engage in over the holidays
linkedLearningAreas: The learner is able to relate the leisure activities with the skills of drawing, painting, dancing and singing in Creative Arts
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: developed as learners listen keenly and actively so as to respond appropriately to questions on leisure time activities
values: Unity: as learners discuss together the leisure time activities that they engage in over the holidays
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Health Promotion: learners engage in appropriate leisure activities for good physical and mental health as they come up with a list of leisure activities that promote healthy living

subStrands.name: Interactive Speaking — Shopping for Food
specificLearningOutcomes: Respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement
Use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions
Exhibit confidence to contribute actively in conversations
keyInquiryQuestions: Where do you buy your food?
learningExperiences: Listen to and repeat names of different shops of food (la boucherie, la boulangerie, l'épicerie, la crèmerie, le café, le restaurant) as they identify different professions related to food (serveur, butcher, chef...)
Pick out vocabulary on quantities of foodstuff (un kilo de, un litre de, un verre de)
Search for different shops of foodstuff using digital devices
Request for food items using appropriate expressions (Je voudrais un paquet du lait, Je voudrais un kilo de la viande, Je voudrais deux pains)
Play games to practice vocabulary related to quantities of food and drinks
linkedLearningAreas: The concept of quantity of food is linked to the concept measurement (weight) in Mathematics
The concept of shopping for food is linked to the concept of budgeting in Business Studies under Pre-Technical Studies
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: developed as learners speak clearly and effectively on food and drinks using appropriate expressions and gestures
values: Responsibility: Learners search for different shops of foodstuffs using digital devices without going to other unnecessary sites
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Career Guidance: Learners explore different career opportunities as they identify different professions related to food

subStrands.name: Oral Expression — Physical Appearance
specificLearningOutcomes: Structure oral communication in a clear and coherent manner
Use gestures and facial expressions to enhance oral communication
Express enthusiasm to engage in oral communication
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should we love our bodies as they are?
learningExperiences: Select different attributes of physical appearances from audio texts (grand, petit, gros, mince)
Listen to and repeat sentences on physical appearance
Play the hot seat game where learners describe each other orally using their physical attributes
Constitute groups of diverse physical appearance and engage in miming activities
Engage in group work activities among diverse learners to bring diversity
linkedLearningAreas: The learner is able to link the concept of physical appearance attributes to qualitative adjectives in English
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: The learners speak clearly and effectively using appropriate language as they describe each other orally using their physical attributes
values: Respect: as learners appreciate diversity in each other's uniqueness in physical appearances while engaging in miming activities
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Social Cohesion: The learners of diverse physical attributes learn to work together through engaging in group work activities

subStrands.name: Active Listening — Seasons
specificLearningOutcomes: Recall key points in spoken communication
Interpret verbal cues from audio stimuli
Demonstrate willingness to be receptive to new ideas in oral interactions
keyInquiryQuestions: How is the weather different in some months of the year?
learningExperiences: Listen to audio clips about seasons in Kenya and the months they occur to pick out new vocabulary (La saison sèche, la saison des pluies, il fait chaud, il pleut, il y a du vent)
Compare seasons and weather patterns of Kenya and France from audio stimuli
Watch audio-visual clips with vocabulary on different types of clothing and categorize them into warm or light clothing (pull, blouson, pantalon, robe, chemise)
Play rhyming games in groups to enhance vocabulary mastery on weather patterns
Play games on vocabulary search on weather and clothing in groups using digital devices (search engine set with "Safe Search ON")
linkedLearningAreas: The concept of vocabulary on weather patterns is related with the concept of weather and climate in Geography under Social Studies
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: The learners listen critically to compare perspectives as they distinguish seasons and weather patterns of Kenya and France
Digital literacy: as learners use the internet effectively to search for the seasons and related weather patterns in France
values: Unity: Learners work in groups as they play rhyming games to enhance vocabulary mastery on weather patterns
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Safety and Security: learners search from safe sites online as they play video games on weather and clothing

subStrands.name: Interactive Speaking — In the Neighbourhood
specificLearningOutcomes: Respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement
Use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions
Use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication
Exhibit confidence to contribute actively in conversations
keyInquiryQuestions: Which landmark best describes your neighbourhood?
learningExperiences: Participate in "Repeat-after-me" exercise to acquire vocabulary on places and facilities in the neighbourhood (la boutique, le marché, l'église, la boulangerie, la mosquée, le supermarché)
Sing songs on items and areas in the neighborhood
Source and watch video clips on locating items (Où est ...? Où sont)
Do simple skits collaboratively on location or position of buildings and facilities in the neighbourhood while respecting each other's opinions (à travers, en face de, à côté de, derrière, près de)
linkedLearningAreas: The concept of locating places and facilities is related to the concept of prepositions and adverbs of place in English
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: as learners speak clearly and effectively using appropriate language, expressions and gestures while engaging in skits of locating places in the neighbourhood
values: Unity: Learners work together in group activities as they sing songs on areas around their neighbourhood
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Interpersonal Relationships: enhanced as learners mutually respect each other's opinions as they do simple skits on locating different places
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 1.0's rubric (shared across all 9 sub-strands) grades ability to use targeted vocabulary/expressions, maintain correct pronunciation/intonation/rhythm/pacing, respond to prompts, employ gestures and facial expressions, and display willingness to participate — confirming non-verbal cues and willingness-to-participate are graded competencies, not just vocabulary recall.

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud — Informal and Other Forms of Greetings
specificLearningOutcomes: Infer meaning of words from simple texts
Read simple texts fluently using the right intonation and pace
Show enthusiasm in reading simple varied texts
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do we read?
learningExperiences: Pick out vocabulary in group on greetings and introductions from digital devices (salut, coucou, ça marche, ça roule, ça gaze ! quoi de neuf ?)
Echo read texts on greetings and introductions in class with the teacher for pronunciation practice
Read texts in pairs to acquire vocabulary (Bonjour, Bonsoir, Tu t'appelles comment? Tu as quel âge ?)
Respond to simple questions from reading texts on informal greetings
Read and rearrange jumbled words to make meaningful sentences
Use dramatic reading of simple texts in small groups for developing fluency (intonation and pace)
Play a skit on self and others' introduction on name, age and where they live
linkedLearningAreas: The learners are able to relate skills on informal greetings and introduction to the same skills in English and Kiswahili
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: developed as the learner reads clearly and effectively using the appropriate articulation, pronunciation, intonation, rhythm and pacing texts on informal greetings
values: Unity: The learner appreciates collaboration in learning while collaboratively reading texts on informal greetings
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Self-esteem: nurtured as the learner confidently introduces him/herself to others

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud — Nuclear Family
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify vocabulary and expressions in texts
Read simple texts for comprehension
Read texts with confidence with support
keyInquiryQuestions: Which was your first storybook to read?
learningExperiences: Read selected passages on families in order to comprehend the use of a wide vocabulary and phrases (age, situation de famille, professions, lieu de travail)
Read passages to extract grammatical structures and key information
Read aloud lyrics of songs about different family setups in French
Answer comprehension questions on family
Compare from visual stimuli different family models and relate to their own
linkedLearningAreas: As the learners engage in role plays they are able to relate the skill of acting with drama in Creative Arts
coreCompetencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The learner comes up with solutions as they infer the meaning of vocabulary from texts
values: Respect: The learners show appreciation for diversity as they sing songs about different family setups in French
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Citizenship: enhanced as the learners take pride in belonging in a family as they relate their families to the different family models

subStrands.name: Reading for Understanding — The Market
specificLearningOutcomes: Summarize key details and facts from the text
Read fluently using the right intonation and pace
Read texts for understanding
keyInquiryQuestions: What do you carry when going shopping?
learningExperiences: Read out a dialogue between a buyer and seller observing the right intonation and pace
Pick out expressions of politeness from texts (s'il vous plaît, excusez-moi, je voudrais... merci)
Read a variety of texts on shopping and point out names of items and their quantities
Read different passages on shopping to compare prices of items
Read simple texts on shopping and point out prices of items and the shops where they can be purchased
linkedLearningAreas: The concept of creating a shopping list is linked to financial literacy in Business Studies under Pre-technical Studies
coreCompetencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The learners learn to prioritize what to buy as they compare the prices of items from texts
values: Respect: nurtured as learners learn to request for items politely when shopping
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Financial Literacy: As learners are sensitized to compare prices of items to make informed choices

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud — Important Dates
specificLearningOutcomes: Decode familiar sounds in words to read simple short texts
Read texts with correct intonation, pace and fluency
Read varied texts with enthusiasm
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should we remember dates of events?
learningExperiences: Read short texts in turns on important dates with fluency
Articulate important dates on calendar (date d'anniversaire, nouvel an, noël, fêtes nationales)
Recite simple poems on numbers
Use the internet appropriately to source for and read vocabulary on important dates
linkedLearningAreas: Learning important dates can be linked to the concept of national holidays in Social Studies
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: developed as learners contribute actively by reading short texts in turns on important dates
values: Responsibility: As learners search vocabulary on important dates from the internet without going to other sites
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Self-esteem: enhanced as learners gain fluency through reading texts on important dates repeatedly

subStrands.name: Reading for Understanding — Leisure Time
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify key details and facts from written texts
Apply information from the text and answer questions
Show an increasing ability to understand words and phrases in context
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do we play different games in school?
learningExperiences: Pick out leisure activities from texts
Match pictures of leisure activities with texts (scrabble, monopoly, vidéo)
Point out expressions of time from texts (le soir, le weekend, les vacances)
Respond to questions from texts on when they undertake leisure activities
Read a variety of written texts about leisure activities (musique, dance, cinéma...)
linkedLearningAreas: The learner is able to relate the leisure activities with the skills of drawing, painting, dancing and singing in Creative Arts
coreCompetencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: as learners answer comprehension questions
values: Love: As learners realize and appreciate that individuals have different gifts, talents and interests
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Health Promotion: Learners are encouraged to engage in appropriate leisure activities to avoid drugs and substance abuse

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud — Shopping for Food
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify vocabulary and expressions from texts
Read texts with correct intonation, pace and fluency
Read varied texts with enthusiasm
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do we quantify food and drinks?
learningExperiences: Read short texts on quantities of foods and drinks
Take turns in reading short texts relating to different shops of food to pick out vocabulary
Match names of shops to different food items
Play word search games on vocabulary related to food quantities and shops
Source for information on quantities of food and different shops from the internet
linkedLearningAreas: The concept of quantity of food is linked to the concept measurement (weight) in Mathematics
The concept of shopping for food is linked to the concept of budgeting in Business Studies under Pre-Technical Studies
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn: developed as learners learn how to read vocabulary on quantities of food and drinks
values: Responsibility: learner develops a sense of responsibility by being able to shop for food
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Life skills: as the learner acquires knowledge on how foods and drinks are quantified

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud — Physical Appearance
specificLearningOutcomes: Decode familiar sounds in words to read simple short texts
Read texts with correct intonation, pace and fluency
Read varied texts with enthusiasm
keyInquiryQuestions: How are we different in physical appearances?
learningExperiences: Echo read short texts on physical appearance in small groups or with the teacher
Source for and read short texts about the physical appearance from the internet
Play word search games on vocabulary related to physical appearance
Use picture stimuli to read about physical appearances
linkedLearningAreas: Pre-Technical studies as learners apply technology in sourcing for information
coreCompetencies: Digital literacy: developed as the learner sources for texts on parts of their body from the internet
values: Responsibility: learner uses the internet responsibly in sourcing for information
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Online safety: as learners use the internet to source for information on physical appearances from safe sites

subStrands.name: Reading Aloud — Seasons
specificLearningOutcomes: Decode familiar sounds in words to read simple short texts
Read texts with correct intonation, pace and fluency
Read varied texts with enthusiasm
keyInquiryQuestions: What precautions should you take in cold weather?
learningExperiences: Echo read texts about seasons, related weather and clothing in small groups for vocabulary
Use the internet to search for texts on clothing items for reading; search engine is set on "safe search"
Engage in interactive read-aloud activities where reading is paused for "question and answer breaks"
Respond to simple questions from read texts about seasons and related weather patterns in groups
Read texts and categorize clothing items according to the weather appropriateness
Use picture stimuli to read and identify seasons according to types of clothing provided
linkedLearningAreas: The concept of vocabulary on weather patterns is related with the concept of weather and climate in Geography under Social Studies
coreCompetencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: developed as learners interpret picture stimuli to relate clothing to seasons
values: Unity: As learners work in groups to source for reading materials from digital devices
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Online safety: as learners search the internet for materials from safe sites

subStrands.name: Guided Reading — In the Neighbourhood
specificLearningOutcomes: Decode familiar sounds in words to read simple short texts
Read texts with correct intonation, pace and fluency
Read varied texts with enthusiasm
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you locate different places in school?
learningExperiences: Echo read texts in small groups to practice intonation and pace in reading
Engage in interactive read-aloud activity where reading is paused for question and answer breaks

Source for texts on different areas and facilities in the neighbourhood from digital devices in small groups and read for vocabulary (la boutique, le marché, l'église, la boulangerie, la mosquée, supermarché)
Read texts and answer questions on location of buildings and facilities in the neighbourhood
Match picture stimuli to given vocabulary about locating areas (à travers, en face de, à côté de, derrière, près de)
linkedLearningAreas: The concept of locating places and facilities is related to the concept of prepositions and adverbs of place in English
coreCompetencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learners develop research skills as they source for texts on different areas in neighbourhood
values: Unity: As learners work in groups to echo read texts
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Online Safety: as learners search the internet for materials from safe sites
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 2.0's shared rubric grades ability to pronounce words in context for accuracy, read with fluency (smoothness, pace, rhythm, intonation) even in texts on unfamiliar topics at the top tier, and analyse simple texts by interpreting and responding to questions using extensive vocabulary — confirming decoding-plus-comprehension, not decoding alone, is the tested competency across all 9 Reading sub-strands.

subStrands.name: Guided Writing — Informal and Other Forms of Greetings
specificLearningOutcomes: Write common words with the correct orthography
Create simple sentences using correct structures
Appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do you greet visitors who come to class?
learningExperiences: Fill crosswords and word puzzles using cues from other texts on greetings and introductions
Fill gaps in simple dialogues using simple vocabulary on greetings and introductions (salut, coucou, ça marche, ça roule, ça gaze ! quoi de neuf ?)
Make sentences from jumbled words to write about greetings and introductions in group activities
Write down dictated simple vocabulary on greetings and introductions
Use visual prompts like pictures and illustrations to write simple texts
linkedLearningAreas: The concept of informal greetings and introduction is linked to the greetings concept in social linguistics in Kiswahili
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: developed as learners work together in group activities
values: Love: enhanced as learners write short greetings to one another
pertinentContemporaryIssues: Life skills: As learners label items for safety and ease of retrieval

subStrands.name: Guided Writing — Nuclear Family

keyInquiryQuestions: What documents require information about your family?
learningExperiences: Fill out forms seeking information on names, nationality, date and place of birth, marital status, residence etc.
Write short emails to friends and classmates about family members and what they do (work) and what they like
Write chats or information on social media platforms using their parents' or teachers' phones
linkedLearningAreas: As the learners engage in role plays they are able to relate the skill of acting with drama in Creative Arts
coreCompetencies: Digital Literacy: as the learners construct coherent texts through use of digital devices
values: Love: as learners write short emails to each other

Correctly match specific items in terms of names, quantities and where in the market they are sold

keyInquiryQuestions: Which dates are important to you?

Make a calendar of events in groups
Match picture stimuli of important days and dates
Fill word puzzles with vocabulary on important dates
linkedLearningAreas: Learning important dates can be linked to the concept of national holidays in Social Studies
coreCompetencies: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: developed as learners fill puzzles and use picture stimuli to carry out tasks

subStrands.name: Guided Writing — Leisure Time

Write texts on leisure, games and sporting activities
Display increased interest to express ideas and information in a coherent and organized manner through writing

values: Social Justice: The learners realize that they have different gifts, talents and interests with equal opportunities

subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand 3.0's shared rubric grades ability to write clear/readable texts (spacing, neatness, individual handwriting style at the top tier) AND ability to use correct language structures/vocabulary (spelling, grammar, sentence structure, context-appropriate vocabulary) as two separate indicators — confirming legibility and grammatical accuracy are both independently assessed, not just vocabulary recall.

notes: Grade 7 French has the same 3-strand / 9-theme structure as Grade 8 (Greetings and Introductions, Family, My Surrounding, Time, Fun and Enjoyment, Foods and Drinks, My Body, Weather and Environment, Getting Around) = 27 distinct sub-strands. Unlike Grade 8, Grade 7's per-theme sub-strand names vary by skill type per theme (e.g. 1.1 Interactive Speaking, 1.2 Oral Expression, 1.3 Interactive Listening, 1.4 Active Listening, 1.5 Listening for Information, 1.6 Interactive Speaking again, 1.7 Oral Expression again, 1.8 Active Listening again, 1.9 Interactive Speaking again) rather than one uniform label per strand — read directly from each theme's own strand table per CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md. Two CSL (Community Service Learning) and cross-subject appendices (Appendix 1: CSL guidelines, Appendix 2: assessment methods/resources/non-formal activities) were reviewed but contain no sub-strand-specific enumerated content beyond what is already captured per sub-strand above.
